advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound child stdout/stderr during the read (incremental read with a hard cap) rather than checking len() after communicate() has already buffered everything.
evidence: `stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=DEADLINE_SECONDS)`
`if len(stdout) > MAX_STDOUT or len(stderr) > MAX_STDERR: raise _Abstain("worker_failure")`
ADR/docs claim bounded stdout/stderr as a hardening property, but the bound is post-hoc, not enforced during the read.
advisory.finding: MAX_STDOUT/MAX_STDERR do not bound peak memory: `proc.communicate(timeout=...)` buffers the child's ENTIRE stdout/stderr into memory before the `len(stdout) > MAX_STDOUT` check runs, so a hostile or runaway terraform-config-inspect can OOM the process despite the stated bound. The limit only rejects the result after it has already been fully read.
scenarios: A pinned binary produces (or a replaced/misbehaving binary produces) multi-GB stdout under the 60s deadline, exhausting host memory before the size check fires.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the redundant `and not _drop_env(k)` from the allowlist comprehension (allowlist is already closed) or add a comment documenting it as a defensive no-op.
evidence: `env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k in _KEEP_ENV and not _drop_env(k)}`
`_KEEP_ENV = frozenset({"LANG", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE", "SYSTEMROOT", "WINDIR", "COMSPEC", "PATHEXT"})`
`_DROP_ENV_PREFIXES` contains TF_, AWS_, HTTP_, GIT_, etc. — none prefix a _KEEP_ENV member.
advisory.finding: Dead/misleading filter clause in `_minimal_env`: `if k in _KEEP_ENV and not _drop_env(k)`. `_KEEP_ENV` is a closed allowlist and none of its members (LANG, LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, SYSTEMROOT, WINDIR, COMSPEC, PATHEXT) match any `_DROP_ENV_PREFIXES` entry, so `not _drop_env(k)` can never be False — the clause is unreachable and obscures the actual (allowlist-only) contract.
scenarios: A future maintainer adds an env var to _KEEP_ENV that happens to collide with a drop-prefix and assumes the drop filter still applies to the allowlist.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `SECRET not in json.dumps({evidence, receipt})` assertion to the match-path test using the secret-laden `_module_json()` payload.
evidence: _module_json embeds the secret: "description": SECRET, "default": SECRET (tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:65-66)

test_exact_declaration_matches_every_supported_class asserts outcome/detail/schema only: 'assert f"class={klass}" in result.evidence["detail"]' and schema validation, with no `SECRET not in json.dumps(...)` check (lines 219-232)

Contrast: test_module_source_equals_matches_by_hash_not_literal DOES assert 'assert "../modules/vpc" not in encoded' (line 247) and fault tests assert 'assert SECRET not in encoded' (line 340), but the generic match path does not
Diff commit message contract: 'child streams, credentials, and Terraform literals never escape into evidence, receipts, or logs.'
advisory.finding: The match-path test (`test_exact_declaration_matches_every_supported_class`) drives the corroborator with the default `_module_json()` payload whose variable `description` and `default` are both set to `SECRET`, yet it never asserts that `SECRET` is absent from `result.evidence`/`result.receipt` — so it cannot detect a regression that leaks a Terraform literal into a positive `match` result, even though the change explicitly contracts that 'child streams, credentials, and Terraform literals never escape into evidence, receipts, or logs.' The fault-path and module_source_equals tests do make this assertion, but the successful-match path (the one that actually returns a location and provenance) does not.
scenarios: A future change to _match_result / match_evidence that folds an entry attribute (e.g. description/default) into the evidence detail or receipt would leak a literal and stay green on the match-path test
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_exact_declaration_matches_every_supported_class, after asserting outcome==MATCH add: `assert SECRET not in json.dumps({"e": result.evidence, "r": result.receipt}, sort_keys=True)`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin and verify an expected SHA-256 (or checksum-file) of the audited terraform-config-inspect binary rather than relying only on source-commit pinning and runtime before/after hashing.
evidence: "GOBIN=\"$RUNNER_TEMP/tfci-bin\" go install \\  github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d"

terraform_corroborator.py records executable version as "unknown" and computes a runtime SHA only for before/after comparison: `before = _sha256_file(exe)` ... `if before != after: raise _Abstain("binary_replaced")`
ABSENCE: no committed expected SHA-256 of the audited binary to compare `_sha256_file(exe)` against
"uses: actions/setup-go@44694675825211faa026b3c33043df3e48a5fa00  # v6.0.0"
"go-version: \"1.25.x\""
"GOBIN=\"$RUNNER_TEMP/tfci-bin\" go install github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d"
ABSENCE: no go.sum, vendor directory, or explicit GOSUMDB/GONOSUMDB/GOFLAGS setting introduced alongside the install step
dropped.finding: The audited terraform-config-inspect binary is installed via `go install ...@<commit-sha>` but no expected binary digest is pinned/verified anywhere; the runtime SHA-256 before/after check only detects mid-run replacement, not that the installed binary matches an audited artifact.
merged_from: The canary job selects Go with a floating patch selector `go-version: "1.25.x"`, so the compiled terraform-config-inspect binary is not reproducible across Go patch releases even at the same upstream source commit.

`go install github.com/hashicorp/terraform-config-inspect@<sha>` resolves and builds the module's transitive dependency graph with no committed go.sum/vendoring or explicit GOFLAGS/checksum-DB posture recorded in the change, leaving transitive-dependency provenance implicit.
scenarios: A future Go toolchain or transitive dependency change at the same source commit produces a different binary that is still accepted as 'audited'.
